policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Micaiah' is a proper-name transliteration that fits either the qere spelling (mikayehu) or the ketiv (mikahu); the English does not distinguish the two orthographies, and the only note (alternative_rendering, 'Or, eunuch') concerns 'officer', not this word. Base qere fallback retained.

ASV 'Turn thy hand' renders a singular noun, matching the qere yadekha (thy hand); the ketiv yadeykha is plural (thy hands), which the ASV does not render. Neither note on the verse (hebrew_gloss 'in his simplicity'; alternative_rendering on the armor) bears on this word.
